TLDR: Italy currently has two houses of government, both with equal power. In order for any legislation to pass, it must pass BOTH houses verbatim or it ends up going back and forth forever. This leads to governmental deadlock, which is a problem for Italy since their economy is in the toilet, govt budget bloated, and banks on the edge of collapse under their current status quo.
That doesn't explain the fall of the EU nor the vote against. I want to know the real reasons.

Here is my understanding:

A yes vote would have given more power to the government. Not only that but it would have been more centralized power.

Italians voted no by about 59% vs yes at 41%. What this 'no' vote shows is that the Italians do not wish to expand the government and disapprove of the current administration's way of doing things. For one thing the economy is in the shitter, and for another there has been a lot of migrants making it to Italy and we all know how that goes.

This no vote tells us that the Italians do not want to continue in the direction they are heading and want change. This change may end up being Italexit. If Italy voted to leave, the EU would almost certainly crumble shortly thereafter.

Do not take my word for this. It has been very difficult to figure out exactly what this referendum was about and even more difficult to decifer the implications of the 'no' vote. This is the conclusion I have reached and I may not be totally correct.
